day1_insight: Recent rain (10 mm over the past few days) is washing urban runoff into the surf — the single biggest cause of beach contamination — especially near storm drains and creek mouths. The model's main signals right now: 10 mm of rain has fallen, washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf; high tide timing is lowering risk — how long before mid-morning the last high tide fell, which sets how much the water has just washed off the upper beach; and low river/creek flow means little watershed runoff is reaching the shore. The last lab sample (20 MPN/100mL) is now 25 days old — beaches are sampled about weekly, so a reading this stale carries little weight, and this estimate leans on current conditions. It's a naturally clean, well-flushed open-coast beach (unsafe only ~3% of the time), so outside of storms it's reliably safe.
